newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France cargo rates must yield profits.
newsitem.headline: Air France cargo rates must yield profits.

text.p: Air France's air freight rates must enable it to operate profitable, its cargo director for Germany Helmut Scherret told Reuters.
"Our rates policy is decided by the profitability of our freighters. That must be ensured and that decides our rates policy so there is a margin," he said.
"How we keep (the rates) in relation to the competition is not decisive," he added.

Air France introduced "moderate increases" in ex-Germany rates on selected routes in mid-October, in particular raising prices on destinations which had been too low compared to the market, such as New York and Shanghai, he noted.
Air France had added a 15 pfennig a kilo fuel surcharge on its ex-Germany cargo rates from November 4, a rate set by most airlines.
Air France only sells cargo space in Germany through agents.
"We have a complete agents policy. The IATA agents have the most important sales role," Scherretsaid. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
